title: Friction Test 3
summary: This lesson explores the physics of friction, a force between two surfaces touching each other that slows moving objects down. Students will learn how surface texture affects friction, how friction produces heat, and how oil reduces friction.

sections.text: Scene: A visual diagram shows two surfaces touching each other, with a moving object being slowed down by the force between them. I wonder...?: What is friction? Answer: Friction is a force between two surfaces touching each other that slows moving objects down.

Scene: A detailed illustration compares rough surfaces and smooth surfaces, highlighting where heat is produced. I wonder...?: How do different surfaces affect friction and what does it produce? Answer: Rough surfaces create more friction than smooth ones, and friction produces heat.

Scene: A close-up view of engine parts shows oil being applied between them to change how they interact. I wonder...?: What can reduce friction between engine parts? Answer: Oil reduces friction between engine parts.

learning_objectives: Define friction and explain how it affects moving objects.
Compare how rough and smooth surfaces create friction.
Identify how heat is produced and how oil reduces friction between engine parts.
